name: GraphQL Storefront
tagline: The same catalog over GraphQL, where a page is one request.
realWorld: A storefront served entirely through GraphQL. The transport's one real advantage over the REST content API is that several root fields travel in one document, so a page that needs three collections of records costs one request instead of three. This profile measures that against the equivalent single-field read. It cannot traverse a relation, because the GraphQL surface exposes the orphan relation column and not the foreign key, so the types carry a denormalized slug instead.

postBody.query: { gql_products(limit: 25) { id title slug price_cents stock } }

traffic.desc: one root field, the GraphQL equivalent of a REST list

postBody.query: { products: gql_products(limit: 25) { id title slug price_cents } collections: gql_collections(limit: 20) { id title slug } reviews: gql_reviews(limit: 25) { id title rating } }

traffic.desc: three root fields in one document, which is the only thing this transport does that REST cannot

postBody.query: { gql_products(limit: 50) { id title slug description price_cents stock collection_slug } }

traffic.desc: a wide selection over 50 records, well inside the measured cost ceiling of 1000

_note: Load-test manifest for this example. Content types are NOT listed here: perf/export-profiles.mjs reads them from the running engine so they cannot drift. Every entry is a POST carrying its own postBody, because each GraphQL request is a document rather than a path: the driver posts it verbatim instead of building a content write. There is no by-id or by-slug entry, because a fixed document cannot take a sampled value and hardcoding a seeded slug would break the moment the seed changes.
